SPEI (development version)

SPEI 1.9.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-23

Changes in results with respect to 1.8.1

Most calls give the same results as in 1.8.1. The ones that change are listed below, with the size of the change found by running the same calls with both versions (script in data-raw/compare-1.8.1.R). Index differences are in index units (z-values); PET differences are relative to the 1.8.1 value.

Calls that give the same results as 1.8.1:

  • <spei> and <spi> with the log-Logistic distribution (the default in <spei>) and fit = "ub-pwm" (the default), at any scale, with any kernel and with or without a reference period.
  • <spi> and <spei> with Gamma or PearsonIII in calendar months whose reference period has no zeros. In the wichita precipitation series (382 months, 4 of them zero) this covers all values at scales 3 and 12.
  • <thornthwaite> and <hargreaves> with a vector, a time series, or a matrix whose number of rows is a multiple of 12.
  • <penman> with Rs or CC, methods ICID and FAO, when the given or estimated solar radiation does not exceed the clear-sky radiation, and when z is given without P or P0.

Calls that give different results:

Function and options Cause Values changed Size of the change
<spi>/<spei>, Gamma or PearsonIII, calendar months with zeros in the reference period #87 All values of those calendar months wichita, SPI-1 Gamma: 91 of 382 values, mean +0.09, max +0.72. The 4 zero months were -Inf and are now finite. A dry-season series with up to 60% zero months: SPI-1 Gamma 365 of 480 values, mean +0.32, max +3.2 (115 -Inf now finite); PearsonIII 432 of 480, mean +0.51; SPI-3 Gamma 186 of 480, mean +0.14. Changes are always upwards: 1.8.1 values were biased toward drought.
<spi>/<spei>, fit = "pp-pwm" or "max-lik" #67 All 1.8.1 returned only NA.
<spi>/<spei>, Gamma or PearsonIII with params pze stored in coefficients All Results now equal those of the call that produced params. In 1.8.1 the difference was masked by #87.
<spi>/<spei>, a series or month that cannot be fitted, in multi-series input or with ref.start #64 Values wrongly set to NA Those values are now computed.
<thornthwaite>, <hargreaves>, <penman>, matrix or array input that is not a time series, with a number of rows that is not a multiple of 12 Calendar of sites after the first was shifted All sites except the first wichita (382 months) as two identical columns: <thornthwaite> second column mean 15%, max 31%; <hargreaves> second column mean 33%, max 74%.
<penman> with P or P0 Clear-sky radiation used a fixed 840 m instead of z Most months wichita (z = 402.6 m) with P: mean -0.3%, max -0.7%. The change grows with the difference between z and 840 m.
<penman>, solar radiation above clear-sky radiation Rs/Rso limited to 1 (FAO-56 eq. 39) Only those months wichita with tsun: 9 of 382 months (Oct 2000 to Jun 2001, where TSUN exceeds the day length), mean +8%, max +29%.
<penman>, method = "ASCE" with RH Vapour pressure from mean of e0(Tmax) and e0(Tmin) All cabinda: mean -0.8%, max -1.1%.
<penman>, <hargreaves>, latitudes above about 66.5 degrees in polar summer Sunset hour angle set to pi Polar-day months 70 degrees N: June +1.8 to 2.0%, July +0.9 to 1.1%. 75 degrees N (<penman>): May +2.9%, June +4.9%, July +3.9%.
<penman> with tsun in polar night; <thornthwaite> for an all-cold site among others; <penman> with 1 or 2 time steps Fixes P5, P6, P8 NA, NaN or an error before Values are now returned.

Other changes in behaviour that can break existing scripts (see below): <penman> requires z, <thornthwaite> requires at least 12 months, scale must be a positive integer, and the coefficients of Gamma and PearsonIII have an extra row pze.

Breaking changes

  • For the Gamma and PearsonIII distributions, $coefficients now has an extra row pze with the probability of zero precipitation in the reference period, and this value is used when the coefficients are passed back through params. Before, pze was re-estimated from the new data, so applying calibrated parameters to other data gave inconsistent values. Arrays without the pze row (from earlier versions) are still accepted, with a warning.
  • <penman> now requires the elevation z. It was optional when P or P0 was given, and a fixed elevation of 840 m was then silently used for the clear-sky solar radiation.

Bug fixes

  • <spei> and <spi>: the adjustment for the probability of zero precipitation (pze) was overwritten for the Gamma and PearsonIII distributions, so zero-precipitation periods were returned as -Inf and non-zero periods were biased toward drier values. This regression was introduced in 1.8.0; log-Logistic was not affected. Thanks to Mark L. Morrissey for reporting it (#87; also #79, #85).
  • <spei> and <spi>: fit = "max-lik" and fit = "pp-pwm" returned only NA. max-lik now uses the ub-pwm estimates as starting values, and pp-pwm passes the plotting-position constants correctly to lmomco::pwm.pp() (#67).
  • <spei> and <spi>: fit = "max-lik" with Gamma or PearsonIII now warns and uses ub-pwm, as documented.
  • <spei> and <spi>: when a month had no data or constant values in one series, values of the same month in the first series (or of another month, when ref.start was set) were set to NA (#64).
  • <penman>, <hargreaves> and <thornthwaite>: with matrix or array input that is not a time series, and a length that is not a multiple of 12, the sites after the first got shifted calendar months (day length and days per month).
  • <penman>: with several sites and P0, the elevations z were recycled along time instead of across sites. z is now also used for the clear-sky radiation when P or P0 is given.
  • <penman> and <hargreaves>: extraterrestrial radiation in polar summer (sun above the horizon all day) used the largest sunset hour angle found in the data instead of pi, underestimating it above about 66.5 degrees.
  • <spei> and <spi>: 3-d arrays with dimnames gave an error.
  • <spei> and <spi>: time series with a non-integer frequency (e.g. 365.25) returned only NA; they now give an error.
  • <spei> and <spi>: with fit = "max-lik", fits where the optimisation found no valid parameters were used anyway; the ub-pwm estimates are now kept, with a warning. <parglo.maxlik> now reports conv = 1 in that case.
  • <hargreaves>: Pre given as a matrix or array failed with “non-conformable arrays” (#59, thanks to Kai Lochbihler).
  • <penman>: with tsun, months of polar night (day length 0) returned NA.
  • <penman>: input with one or two time steps failed with “subscript out of bounds” (#75).
  • <thornthwaite>: with several sites, a site with all monthly means below 0 C got NaN instead of zero.
  • <kern>: kern(1, "gaussian") returned NaN.
  • <penman>: the ratio Rs/Rso in the net longwave radiation term is now limited to 1, as in FAO-56 eq. 39.
  • <penman>: with method = "ASCE" and RH, the actual vapour pressure was computed from the saturation pressure at mean temperature instead of the mean of the saturation pressures at maximum and minimum temperature (ASCE-EWRI 2005, eq. 41).
  • <kern.plot> restores the graphics parameters it changes.
  • <plot.spei>: colours were assigned by factor order with inverted labels, so a series with only negative (or only positive) values was drawn entirely in the wet colour (#72).
  • <plot.spei>: the y-axis label was taken from the deparsed call, so it failed when spi/spei were called under another name and could give the wrong label with do.call(). The index name is now stored in the object ($index).
  • <plot.spei>: the shading of the reference period started one month late and assumed monthly data.
  • <plot.spei>: every plot gave a “Removed n rows containing missing values” warning.
  • <summary.spei>: the fitted values were printed once per series.

Other changes

  • <spei> and <spi>: the Gamma and PearsonIII distributions now warn when the data contain negative values, which they cannot fit.
  • <thornthwaite> now requires at least 12 months of data. With fewer, the annual heat index was computed from a partial year without notice (#68).
  • <spei>, <spi>, <penman>, <hargreaves> and <thornthwaite> report the computation options with message() instead of print(), so they can be silenced with suppressMessages() as well as with verbose = FALSE (#61). <spi> now names the SPI, not the SPEI, in this report and in $info.
  • <spei> and <spi> warn when periods of the year could not be fitted (fewer than 4 non-zero values, or constant values, in the reference period) and were set to NA (#76, #77).
  • <spei> and <spi>: scale must be a positive integer no larger than the length of the series. Before, non-integer values were accepted, 0 gave a misleading error, and a scale longer than the series returned only NA.
  • Clearer errors for malformed arguments: an unnamed kernel list, na.rm or verbose set to NA, params that is not a 3-d array, and an unknown method in <penman>. A kernel shift given as an integer (0L) is now accepted.
  • Tests no longer depend on R’s English error messages.
  • <plot.spei> has a main argument for a title, and the y-axis breaks cover the full range of values instead of stopping at -2 and 2 (#38). The documentation explains that the methods are called as plot(x), summary(x) and print(x) (#78).
  • The dependency on the retired reshape package has been removed.
  • Unused imports and the unused internal function pglo() were removed.

Documentation

  • Documentation of the PET functions revised: P is not a constant but is computed from z when missing; z is required by <penman>; U2 must be wind speed at 2 m (no height conversion is done); the CO2 correction is applied to both reference crops; minimum input lengths; and the Thornthwaite method does not use the original table for temperatures of 26.5 ºC or more. The Hargreaves equation is now cited as Hargreaves and Samani (1985) (#86).
  • Dataset documentation corrected: YEAR and MONTH in wichita, wind speed units (m s-1) in wichita and cabinda, the source of cabinda, and the country of Lahore in balance.
  • Licence field changed from GPL-2 to GPL (>= 2), matching the “version 2 or later” terms stated in the README and package documentation.
  • README: licence badge, repository links and a reference fixed; the version history now points to NEWS.md.
  • wichita dataset: TSUN was missing from the documentation (ACSH was listed twice), and five TSUN values between October 2000 and May 2001 exceed the possible day length; this is now noted.

SPEI 1.8.1, July 2023

CRAN release: 2023-03-02

  • Maintenance release with fixes for changes in R-devel, required by CRAN.

SPEI 1.8.0, November 2022

CRAN release: 2023-01-20

This is a major release that adds a range of substantial new features and fixes a number of major and minor bugs.

Breaking changes

  • All functions now accept 3-d arrayed data, enabling the possibility of using them on gridded climate data. A new data set (cruts4) has been added to test this new function.
  • Function <spei> now accepts non-monthly data (that is, data with frequency other than 12).
  • A thorough set of test functions have been implemented to help developing new functions without compromising the old results (Thanks to Doug Freedman who wrote the seminal set of tests).

New features

  • More thorough data and options checks have been implemented, and a single error / warning message is produced containing all the errors upon failure.
  • Different verbosity levels are now implemented in all functions: now they print information about the options being used. A new argument (verbosity) can be used to override this behavior if not wanted.
  • Different versions of the Penman-Monteith ETo calculation have been implemented in function <penman>.
  • A new option to include CO2 concentration data is now available in function <penman>.
  • A new option for when no wind data are available in function <penman>.
  • <plot.spei> has been completely rewritten based on ggplot2, solving some bugs and enabling more flexibility.

Bug fixes

  • Several minor bugs in <thornthwaite>, <hargreaves>, and <penman> functions have been solved (output difference is less than 0.1%).
  • A bug in <spei> has been solved that resulted in bad cumulative data when using a non-rectangular kernel, leading to incorrect SPEI values.

SPEI 1.7.2, June 2019 (only on GitHub).

Breaking changes

  • Allowing for data with frequency other than 12 in <spei> function.

SPEI 1.7.1, June 2017.

Bug fixes

  • Corrected an error in <spei> function, which was not working when distribution was Gamma or PeasonIII and using user provided parameters. (Thanks to Emanuele Cordano, emanuele.cordano@gmail.com – ‘ecor’)
  • Added probability of monthly precipitation = 0 (pze) when using user provided parameters. (Thanks to Emanuele Cordano).

SPEI Version 1.7, June 2017.

CRAN release: 2017-06-07

Bug fixes

  • Corrected a bug in the function which resulted in a multiplicative kernel instead of an additive one such the one expected in the and functions.
  • Plotting methods for objects completely rewritten, now using . Additionally, a bug causing a bad representation of time series starting in months other than January has been corrected.

SPEI 1.6, September 2013.

CRAN release: 2013-11-07

Bug fixes

  • Corrected an error in the function which resulted in wrong potential evapotranspiration estimates when a multivariate time series was used as input.
  • Corrected an error in the function which resulted in wrong handling of zero precipitation months when using the Gamma or PearsonIII distribution.
  • Minor fixes to the and functions to correctly handle objects when they result from a call to .
  • Modification to the function, which now yields kernel coefficients averaging one.
  • Corrected an error in the functions and which resulted in ub-pwm method being used irrespective of the value of the parameter used, when using the ‘Gamma’ or ‘PearsonIII’ distributions.
  • Minor changes to the documentation.

SPEI 1.5, May 2013.

Bug fixes

  • Optimization of function , now using embed() for accumulating the data at the desired time scale.

SPEI 1.4, May 2013.

CRAN release: 2013-05-09

Bug fixes

  • Minor fixes to functions and .
  • Documentation of the function defined by mistake ed as the saturation vapor pressure, while it should read ‘actual vapor pressure’.
  • Function added to display basic information about the SPEI package at startup.
  • Function added to display the NEWS file.

SPEI 1.3, March 2013.

CRAN release: 2013-03-08

Bug fixes

  • Minor fixes to functions and .
  • Added new option for user-supplied SPEI parameters in the function. This overrides the fitting of a probability function to the data.
  • Added new dataset from Allen et al. (1998).

SPEI 1.2, October 2012.

CRAN release: 2012-03-21

Bug fixes

  • Fixed a bug causing several functions to fail when a time series not belonging to matrix class was provided.
  • Function now distinguishes between calls to and and labels the axis accordingly.

SPEI 1.1, March 2012.

CRAN release: 2012-01-25

  • Functions and now yield an object of class “spei”.
  • New functions for summarizing and plotting “spei” objects are provided.
  • An option to establish a reference period for the computation of the indices has been implemented in functions and .

SPEI 1.0, January 2012.

CRAN release: 2011-10-18

First release of the SPEI package.
